title: Find water outdoors
summary: Pick the safest source you can find, and treat it anyway.

cards.headline: Even in the cold, you need about 2 liters a day
cards.body: You lose water through sweat, breathing, cold, and stress. Finding water is one of your most urgent jobs.

sources.title: FM 21-76 / MCRP 3-02F Survival, ch. 6: Water procurement
ATP 3-50.21 Survival, ch. 3: Water

cards.headline: Pick moving water over still water
cards.body: Flowing water is usually a better choice than still, stagnant water. Avoid water that smells bad, looks dark, or has floating material. Treat it either way.

cards.headline: Catch rain in clean containers
cards.body: Set out clean, nonporous containers or a tarp to catch rain as it falls. Treat it before drinking when you can, and always treat rain that ran off leaves or plants.

cards.headline: Mop up morning dew with cloth around your ankles
cards.body: Before sunrise, tie cloth or fine grass around your lower legs and walk through tall, wet grass. Wring it into a container. Treat it before drinking.

cards.headline: Melt snow before you drink it
cards.body: Eating unmelted snow lowers your body temperature. Melt it first, near a fire or in a container under your outer layers, then treat it like any other wild water.

cards.headline: A solar still can supply all the water you need
cards.body: A ground still makes about half a liter to a liter a day. You'd need at least three to meet one person's daily need. Treat it as a backup, not a plan.

cards.headline: Which wild water should you treat before drinking?
cards.body: Clear and clean-looking water can still carry germs.
